failure_summary.description: Agents imported tools from a nonexistent `tools` module instead of calling the injected functions directly.
Agents searched for attractions but did not save the newly generated results to the cache.
Agents missed information supplied in context or in replies to clarification questions, including traveler counts and requested amenities.
Agents failed to use an overall trip span to plan the return flight and, where applicable, derive lodging dates from the same trip.
An upper arrival-time bound was encoded as an exact time rather than an interval.

patch.reasoning: The skill already explicitly prohibits importing tools and requires saving new results, so those repeated failures do not reveal a content gap worth duplicating. The edits clarify how to interpret a clearly stated trip span, how to encode one-sided time bounds, and how to apply values supplied in clarification replies to hotel searches or cached results.

edits.target: - Preserve user-provided dates, entity values, and casing. For a round trip, make two separate flight searches: one outbound and one with the route reversed for the return. Use each leg’s date as its `departure_date`; do not represent the return leg by setting `arrival_date` on the outbound search. Ask for an unknown endpoint rather than assuming a route. When a hotel stay is given as a check-in date plus an unambiguous duration in nights rather than a checkout date, call `adjust_date(date=<check-in date>, delta_days=<number of nights>)` and use its returned date as checkout; do not treat the duration as missing.
edits.content: - Preserve user-provided dates, entity values, and casing. For a round trip—including when the wording clearly gives the overall trip span from one date through another—search the outbound leg and a separate return leg with the route reversed. Use each leg’s date as its `departure_date`; do not represent the return leg solely by setting `arrival_date` on the outbound search. Ask for an unknown endpoint rather than assuming a route. For lodging clearly tied to the same trip, use the stated trip start as check-in when it is the intended start of the stay. When the hotel stay is given as a check-in date plus an unambiguous duration in nights rather than a checkout date, call `adjust_date(date=<check-in date>, delta_days=<number of nights>)` and use its returned date as checkout; do not treat the duration as missing.

edits.target: Treat stated soft preferences as actionable: translate a standard time-of-day preference without exact bounds into a reasonable interval in the expected format (for example, afternoon as `12:00 PM`–`5:00 PM`).
edits.content: For a one-sided time bound, encode the full interval rather than a single exact time: “by T” means midnight through T, and “after T” means T through the end of the day, using the time format expected by the tool.

edits.target: - Resolve brief affirmations such as “yes” against the immediately preceding assistant question or proposal, and carry forward the proposed entity or category as stated.
edits.content: - Treat replies to clarification questions as active plan inputs even when they are not phrased as new requests. Map a stated traveler count to `num_people` for hotel searches or filters, and map each explicitly requested amenity to its matching schema field. If a compatible cached result lacks these criteria, retrieve and filter it, then save the updated result.
